title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 — Section 32 (Termination of proceedings)

content.overview: The arbitral proceedings are terminated by the final arbitral award or by an order of the arbitral tribunal under section 32(2). The tribunal shall issue a termination order where the claimant withdraws the claim (unless the respondent objects and has a legitimate interest in a final settlement), the parties agree on termination, or continuation has become unnecessary or impossible. Subject to sections 33 and 34(4), the mandate of the tribunal terminates with the proceedings.
content.glance: Proceedings end by final award or tribunal termination order; mandate ends with proceedings subject to ss. 33 and 34(4).
content.study: Termination is by final award or by a s. 32(2) order. Grounds for a termination order are claim withdrawal (with respondent-objection safeguards), party agreement, or unnecessary/impossible continuation. The mandate ends with the proceedings subject to ss. 33 and 34(4).

questionsAndAnswers.question: How do arbitral proceedings terminate under section 32?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: By the final arbitral award or by a tribunal order under section 32(2) on withdrawal, agreement, or unnecessary/impossible continuation.
